exp0: Core behaviour reproduced. Uniform-positive kernels drive global coherence and topological simplification (flat: r = 0.77, 5 vortices); Mexican-hat kernels fragment the field and proliferate defects (r = 0.02, 244 vortices). Mode selection: 2 of 3 of the source's tabulated mode-selecting kernels reproduce - checkerboard peaks at k = (16, 24), pinwheel at k = (1, 0), traveling-wave mode drift 0.00 Hz against the pinwheel's 0.00 Hz. Not reproduced: traveling_wave_kernel_travels. Per XI.9 the tabulated kernel values come from tools on a different scale convention, so this is evidence about those specific numbers rather than about the implementation - the load-bearing simplifier/complexifier contrast above does reproduce. Note that 5-MeO-like and DMT-like kernels are ordered correctly relative to each other but both sit below the coherence threshold at this coupling strength, because energy matching costs a mixed-sign kernel much of its net coupling.
exp1: In the forced-coherence regime (r_global >= 0.7 - the regime Model B is actually about, since below it nothing is being forced) the tree carries 1.22x the lattice's dissonance at matched coherence - in the predicted direction, but small. The claim is regime-specific, not general: below r_global = 0.7 the same ratio is 0.86, and the *peak* dissonance the three geometries can reach is near-identical (0.99x tree over lattice), so the version of the prediction stated in IX.7 - much higher dissonance on the tree than the lattice at the same drive - does not hold. Only the refined version does. On the defect claim the two readouts disagree, which is informative: local incoherence is 1.21x higher at branch points than a degree-matched null predicts, but IX.5's own statistic - the phase step from a parent segment to the mean of its daughters - is 0.86x the same step along ordinary chain segments, i.e. no larger at branch points at all. Branch points show more neighbourhood disagreement simply because they have more neighbours; the phase discontinuity Model B predicts them to carry is not there.
exp2: Onset is abrupt (peak/mean |dD/dA| = 3.6); both branches peak at the same drive amplitude, so there is no bistability to speak of (signed loop area -0.06 of the forward curve, largest branch separation 26% - note the area statistic largely self-cancels on a unimodal curve, which is why the peak shift is quoted first). An attack (a rise in D worth the name) occurs in A=3 100%, A=4 100%, A=6 100% of driven windows; where one occurs, the fraction of the window it holds above half its own peak is A=3 -> 72%, A=4 -> 77%, A=6 -> 35%, peaking at A = 4. Outside that band the tree entrains completely and D collapses to transients at the drive edges, so the model produces a sustained high-dissonance attack only at *partial* entrainment. That is a sharp and counterintuitive prediction: increasing the hypothalamic drive further should abort the attack rather than worsen it. Spontaneous termination (D peaks early and returns to baseline while the drive is still at full amplitude) occurred in 0 of 27 driven windows, so attacks essentially end only when the drive does - the gap IX.7 anticipated.
exp3: Change in D during the intervention, relative to the untreated arm on the same seeds: DMT (Mexican-hat) -52% (+/-8%), 5-MeO (uniform-positive) -2% (+/-9%, within seed noise), oxygen -7% (+/-14%, within seed noise), sumatriptan -13% (+/-8%, within seed noise). Across the full oxygen sweep the response is monotone and contracting sigma_omega reduces dissonance: D = 0.1->0.100, 0.25->0.152, 0.5->0.201, 0.75->0.201, 1->0.228, a 56% reduction at the strongest contraction. That is the direction VI.2 proposes - stabilising the natural frequencies widens the basin of the consonant state - though note VI.2 offers it as a role assignment, not a derivation, and the model was not built to test it. The DMT/5-MeO ordering matches Model B and the clinical anomaly in IV.1: the complexifier relieves and the symmetriser does not, from kernel shape alone, since the two are energy-matched. Onset is scored as the drive amplitude at which D first reaches half the baseline kernel's peak (0.114); baseline crosses at A = 2.33. Persistent kernel shifts that raise that threshold: mexican_hat (A = 4.82, peak D 0.52x baseline).
exp4: At the strongest stimulation, the consonant stack changes D by +0.0740, the source's matched dissonant stack by +0.0554, and a grossly inharmonic golden-ratio stack by +0.0203 (seed spread ~0.0374). Consonant and dissonant stimulation are NOT meaningfully separated, so the one prediction unique to STV rather than to generic desynchronisation does not reproduce here. The grossly inharmonic control does not separate either, so the null is about the entrainment mechanism itself, not about the fineness of the source's mistuning: driving a peripheral branch simply does not move this metric whatever its consonance. That is the stronger negative result of the two.
exp5: Under noise injection LZ rises by +0.44 while D falls by -0.0169 - the asymmetry/antisymmetry distinction behaving exactly as III.1 requires. Pooled across all 45 runs the D-LZ correlation is r = -0.18 (Spearman -0.13); within arms it is -0.85 under noise and +0.49 under drive. Those two carry opposite signs, which is the strongest available form of the result: the same pair of metrics moves together under one manipulation and apart under the other, so no monotone function relates them. The dissonance index is therefore measuring structured incommensurability rather than entropy - prediction 4 in the falsification table, and the precondition for anything else here meaning anything.
exp6: Drive variant: the pacemaker reaches peak D = 0.228 and the diffuse (small-world) drive 0.087; IX.3 is right that they are not equivalent, and the difference is visible at matched achieved coherence, not just at matched amplitude. K_SW: D ranges 0.002 to 0.228 over [-3, 3], peaking at K_SW = 0. Drive frequency: D ranges 0.021 to 0.192 as Omega sweeps 2.8-11.2 Hz, peaking at 4.76 Hz against omega_0 = 5.6 Hz. Size: D varies 86% across N = [225, 625, 1225], so the results MAY be size-dependent - treat the absolute values with caution.
